name: Montenegrin Kačamak
description: Kačamak, a hearty mountain porridge, genuinely combines real mashed potato into the cornmeal along with cheese, making it distinctly heartier than cicvara, its lighter cousin - real technique mixes everything together while hot into a thick, cohesive mass, traditionally topped with sour milk or yogurt to balance its richness.
steps_detailed: Whisk the cornmeal into 1 cup boiling salted water and cook, stirring constantly, 12-15 minutes, until very thick.

Mix in the mashed potato, cheese, and butter while everything is still hot, combining into a thick, cohesive mass - real kačamak is distinctly heartier than cicvara because of this real potato addition.
Top with the yogurt before serving.

name: Montenegrin Cicvara
description: Cicvara, a real creamy cornmeal dish lighter than kačamak, is genuinely cooked in milk rather than water alone, real technique stirring clockwise as it thickens - a small but consistently mentioned detail across real recipes - with the cheese folded in only at the very end so it melts into real distinct, silky pockets rather than dissolving completely.
steps_detailed: Bring the milk and 0.5 cup water to a boil.
Whisk in the cornmeal and cook, stirring in one consistent (traditionally clockwise) direction, 12-15 minutes, until thickened and smooth.
Stir in the butter, then fold in the cheese right at the end, off the heat, so it melts into real distinct pockets rather than dissolving completely into the porridge.

name: Montenegrin Njeguški Pršut Style Beef
description: Njeguški pršut, real dry-cured smoked ham from the village of Njeguši, gets its distinctive flavor from mountain air, sea breeze, and slow beechwood smoking - beef stands in here as a simply seasoned, smoky-style approximation.
steps_detailed: Rub the beef with the paprika and garlic, being generous with the paprika for real smoky depth.
Pan-sear or grill, 2-3 minutes per side, until well charred.

name: Montenegrin Burek
description: Burek, a spiral savory pastry with a meat filling, is shared across the wider Balkans and a genuine Montenegrin staple, real technique rolling the filled dough into a tight coil.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion until soft, 3-4 minutes, then add the beef and pepper and brown, 6-7 minutes. Drain any excess liquid.
Brush each phyllo sheet with oil, spread a thin layer of filling along one edge, and roll into a tight log.
Coil the rolled logs into a spiral in a round baking dish.
Bake at 375F (190C) for 30-35 minutes until deeply golden and crisp.

name: Montenegrin Ćevapi
description: Ćevapi, small grilled meat fingers, shares real roots with Bosnian and wider Balkan tradition, real technique kneading the meat well and shaping it into small finger-sized logs.
steps_detailed: Mix the beef with the garlic, pepper, and salt, kneading by hand 5 minutes until cohesive.
Shape into small finger-sized logs.
Grill over medium-high heat, turning, 6-8 minutes, until well charred and cooked through.

name: Montenegrin Grilled Fish
description: Grilled fish rubbed with garlic and lemon, reflecting Montenegro's rich Adriatic coastal fishing tradition.
steps_detailed: Rub the fish with the garlic and lemon juice, and let sit 10 minutes.
Grill or broil, 4-5 minutes per side, until just cooked through.

name: Montenegrin Cucumber Tomato Salad
description: A simple, bright cucumber and tomato salad topped with real crumbled cheese, shared across the wider Balkans.
steps_detailed: Toss the cucumber and tomatoes with the olive oil.
Top with the crumbled feta.

name: Montenegrin Roasted Almonds
description: A simple roasted almond snack, common across Montenegro.
steps_detailed: Toast the almonds in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring often, 4-5 minutes, until fragrant.

name: Montenegrin Beef and Vegetable Stew
description: A simple, hearty beef and vegetable stew, common Montenegrin home cooking outside the specific named dishes.
steps_detailed: Brown the beef with the onion, 8-9 minutes.
Add the carrot, potato, and tomatoes, and simmer 30-35 minutes until tender.
